en: Making his bannered charger rear,
Sary Khan came into battle,
Destroying all who crossed his path.
Every ridge rang with cries;
The teeming countless host—
Mighty Sary Khan
Drove them back in confusion.
He routed them without leaving one behind
And drove them to the riverbank,
When, from a spur where the mountain vanished,
My broad-backed bay horse looming beneath him,
The slave Kyyaz appeared.
“What wrong have these countless people done?
Is not the khan of this black-hearted rabble
A fool himself?
I shall hew off with an axe
The head of Kyyaz, son of Bagysh;
If any of my former strength remains,
I shall bring such battle upon
This mad fool marked for death
That, turning back from Jeti-Özön,
He will never come again;
I shall fight the villain
And ensure he never returns!
I shall make him unable to cross
The forked pass and barren slope;
I shall make him unable to march
His agitated host through Talas!”
Sary Khan wheeled across his path
And turned his bannered charger’s head;
With his stout and mighty patterned spear,
Aiming straight at brave Kyyaz,
He thundered forward with leveled lance.
At that moment, brave Kyyaz,
When he saw Sary Khan,
Lost the strength in his wrists,
And the courage in his heart;
His ribs trembled,
And, unable to endure it, brave Kyyaz
Felt his fly-like soul quiver.
His strength failed and his power deserted him;
Over a saddle-shaped ridge
Brave Kyyaz fled,
Keeping beyond your uncle Sary’s reach;
Brave Kyyaz escaped,
Despairing of his precious life,
His face drained of color.
To the hero Kanchoro
Brave Kyyaz came alive.
When he reached Kanchoro,
A heavy exchange of gunfire began;
The vast black host of Jediger,
Surging in from every side,
Rescued their khan,
The hero Kyyaz.
Sary Khan raged,
As if inspired with wisdom from the unseen.
Having lost his wits, brave Kyyaz
Pleaded with Kanchoro:
“You are both my comrade and my friend;
We are out of options—give me counsel!
The moon has darkened and night has fallen;
This is a day of terrible calamity.
My strength is spent and my power is gone;
My wits have fled and abandoned me.
From the day I became Kyyaz,
From the day I mounted the horse called Kyyaz,
I have never met my death.
Your dear friend Kyyaz
Has never seen such a man among the people.
I have seen an extraordinary warrior,
One who never yields his companion’s life;
His speech is unlike that of other men,
And his eyes are as large as cups.
He is a champion and a lion,
A hero surpassing all mortals.
Beneath him he has a thoroughbred steed,
And the strength to swallow not only Jediger
But the whole world.
Beside Sary Khan,
Black Maar, who can suck up land across six ravines,
Seems an easy foe.
When I see Sary Khan,
My whole body bristles;
Like a charcoal-burner set ablaze,
He roars like a great drum.
No man can face him in combat;
Whoever encounters him cannot survive.
Even if all Jediger rose as one
And swarmed him, they could not prevail;
Whoever engages
His towering hound cannot escape alive.
He is a champion and a lion,
A hero worth the whole world.
Jediger cannot overcome him;
Why did Almighty God
Create mankind weak
And call us His servants?
My dear khan and comrade,
I will not advance against Sary Khan;
If I fight that branded boar,
I will not survive.
I will not face that madman;
If I confront him, I will not live.
Of all men ever born,
His weight and might are greatest.
Can anyone who grapples with him survive?
Can anyone defeat him face-to-face?
Can one confront him and return alive?
He is bald as a slave-boar,
And few men can wrestle him,
For he is like a champion who could wreck the world.
If Sary Khan truly wished,
He could pluck off this head like a sparrow
And tuck it into his purse.
No man can face him;
No one can bring harm upon him.
Let us send word to the strongest
Among the many heroes of the people;
Let us withhold none, but summon them all,
Then lie down before Sary Khan
And surrender.
His speech is unlike other men’s,
His eyes unlike any human eyes.
What manner of warrior was Semetey,
Who subdued such a man
And brought him here?
When Sary Khan charges in fury,
Our warriors lose their strength.
Without quarrel or strife,
Let us turn back—heed me;
Let us preserve this vast people from slaughter
And remain safe and sound.
My dear comrade, listen to me;
Let us return safely to Jeti-Özön
And lead the bay horse
Before my uncle Sary Khan.
Let us make peace as equals,
And each depart safely to his own land.”
So brave Kyyaz spoke,
Terrified of Sary Khan,
Addressing Chubak’s son Choro
With these words;
Before Kanchoro
Kyyaz made his plea.
As though stabbed in a tender gland,
Kanchoro flared up on hearing this
And sprang down:
“Damn him—Sary Khan
Is a bald charcoal burner.
His greatness and his khanly rank
Are scarcely lower than mine.
Rather than fear Sary Khan,
What if you should behold him, Jediger?
What if you are slaughtered
To the last man, Jediger?
Jeti-Özön is your land,
Or so you keep claiming.
May the earth swallow you, Kyyaz!
I had thought you were a warrior.
I will say, ‘I was mistaken; I submit,’
And return to the bloodthirsty one.
Just watch, Jediger,
And see how I bring about your ruin.
I shall capture you, mount you on a horse,
And take you as a gift
To the fierce wolf, the son of Manas;
By one means or another I shall make peace,
And reconcile myself with him.
After that, Jediger,
I shall decide what to do with you.
You will not rally when I cheer you on;
You Jediger swine will never prosper.
You will not rise when I give you courage;
No Jediger will ever prosper.
You call Sary Khan formidable
And fear a bald woodcutter.
You were a marksman and a warrior—
Now prove your marksmanship.
Make your utmost effort, brave Kyyaz;
There is a broad stone by the lone road—
Hide behind that broad stone.
Once hidden behind it,
He has words no man can fathom,
And many things he could say;
Between his two eyes
He has a red mole as large as a bowl.
Aim at that red mole and fire;
Shoot the cur dead!
For if you do not kill him that way,
Spears cannot pierce him,
Heavy muskets cannot punch through him,
And rifle balls cannot penetrate him—
His invulnerability is indeed real.
That he advanced through Chin-Machin, Kakan, and Beijing
Is also true.
That the accursed man never yielded
His companion’s life is also true.
That bald Sary struck down
The spearmen is also true;
That the firebrand stood
At the foot of the banner is also true.
This Sary Khan will not simply vanish;
Unless Sary Khan is gone,
Jediger’s cause will never prosper.
This hero Sary Khan
Has every cunning of an infidel,
And every kind of stratagem.
He was the mighty khan of the Argyn,
A champion and a lion;
When he entered battle against a clashing foe,
He was the man who bore the banner.
He never panicked on hearing tidings,
Nor stood watching without joining battle.
He never lay quietly upon the earth;
Thrown into fire, he would not burn,
Thrown into water, he would not sink.
His valor was extraordinary;
He was truly a mainstay.
Sary Khan, the champion bound to one’s back,
Was truly a warrior.
His wisdom reaches far;
He is a surpassingly gifted sage.
Whenever he assails an enemy,
He emerges alone at the head of the race.
Sary Khan, the champion bound to one’s back,
Has the thoroughbred bannered charger.
Sary Khan has strength enough
To subdue the whole world.
His eyes see from afar;
Many enemies have wearied themselves fighting him.
He reads the stars in the heavens,
That companion of mighty Semetey.
Damn you, brave Kyyaz—fire at the spot
I have just shown you;
Fire at the lone mole as large as a pail.
Do not look around;
If you are a man, if you are a lion,
If you truly are the hero Kyyaz,
Shoot at the very spot I showed you.
If Sary Khan dies—
If that Sary Khan dies—
It means God has granted him to us.
But if Sary Khan does not die,
They will fight like immortals
Until the brittle reeds ripen
And the ashes of judgment scatter;
The maddened slaves will keep attacking.
No man can defeat him by rushing him,
And he never yields his companion’s life—
Such is the nature of Sary Khan.”
Carried away, Kanchoro spoke,
Standing there and roaring,
While Kyyaz merely stood.
Kyyaz had lost his senses,
And his whole body trembled.
